title: LayoutPlan
description: The AI's plan for a room, before any product is chosen or anything is placed (5.4 L2). This is the tool-schema Claude fills in. It is intent only: categories, priorities, budget shares and relations. Geometry is the solver's job, so nothing here carries a coordinate.

room_type.description: User-selected or inferred. Drives the default budget ratios and the category vocabulary.

slots.description: One furniture opportunity each. Capped at 10 in V1 (5.4 post-checks).

category.description: Must exist in the category vocabulary; checked deterministically after the call, never trusted.

priority.description: Drop order when the room or the budget runs out: nice first, must last.

budget_share.description: Fraction of budget. Renormalised to 100% with a 5% reserve after the call, so the model's arithmetic is never load-bearing.

intent.description: What the slot wants, in terms the solver's candidate generators understand. Every id referenced is checked against the RoomModel before use.

anchor.description: What this slot is positioned relative to: a wall, an opening, or another slot.

relation.description: Closed list: these map one-to-one onto the solver's candidate-pose generators (5.4 L5.2). A relation the solver cannot generate poses for is worse than no relation at all.

facing.description: What the item's front should point at.

notes.description: Free text for the solver's scoring hints and for explaining the plan. Never parsed as geometry.

rationale.description: Short, shown to the user. Why this set of furniture for this room.
